question.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by 

$$
f(X)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡(det(X)).
$$

 
What is the gradient of $f$ with respect to $X$ at $X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The gradient of a function $f:{R}^{m\times n}\to R$ with respect to a matrix $X\in {R}^{m\times n}$ is

$$
{∇}_{X}f(X)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{11}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{12}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1n}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{21}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{22}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{m1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{m2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{mn}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(X)$ where $X=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{11} & {x}_{12} \\ {x}_{21} & {x}_{22}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{2\times 2}$, we get

$$
f(X)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡(det(X))=-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}).
$$

So, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,{∇}_{X}f(X) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{11}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{12}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{21}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{22}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{11}}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{12}}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{21}}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21})) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{22}}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}_{22}}{{x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}} & \frac{{x}_{21}}{{x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}} \\ \frac{{x}_{12}}{{x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}} & \frac{-{x}_{11}}{{x}_{11}{x}_{22}-{x}_{12}{x}_{21}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{X}f(X)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{-4-(-3)} & \frac{1}{-4-(-3)} \\ \frac{-3}{-4-(-3)} & -\frac{(-1)}{-4-(-3)}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{-1} & \frac{1}{-1} \\ \frac{-3}{-1} & -\frac{(-1)}{-1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
